title: California AI Transparency Act (SB 942) -- Generative AI Provenance Disclosure, Effective January 1, 2026
context: 2026-08-27 engine cycle -- SB 942 provenance disclosure duties have been binding since January 1, 2026; California's operational transparency mandate for large generative AI systems
body: California's AI Transparency Act (SB 942) makes provenance disclosure a binding duty, not a best practice. From January 1, 2026, a covered provider of a generative AI system -- one with more than one million monthly users or visitors -- must make a free AI detection tool available to the public so a user can query whether image, video, or audio content was created or altered by that system, and must offer to embed latent provenance disclosures in generated content. The Council of AI reads this as a measurement problem, not a checkbox. A provenance marker that is self-asserted by the generator proves nothing; a marker that carries an independent signature -- a verified measurement credential over the generation record -- lets a downstream auditor confirm who generated what without trusting the generator's own word. That is the same boundary-instrumentation posture the Council of AI applies to synthetic-output marking under the EU AI Act: monitored containment, not provable isolation. Disclosure does not prove content is harmless; it proves the provenance path is watched and verifiable. Concretely: (1) every synthetic-output surface should emit a machine-readable provenance record carrying model identity, generation timestamp, and origin attestation. (2) That record should be independently signed so the disclosure is auditable. (3) The signing chain should feed the Council Signal Containment Incident Index, so an unmarked or mislabeled output is traceable to a boundary event rather than lost in the stream.
